subsystems.name: Magnetic tap
subsystems.role: grips the star's outer plasma and pulls it away from the surface.

subsystems.name: Power supply
subsystems.role: lifting matter out of a stellar gravity well costs a large share of the star's own output.

subsystems.name: Plasma channel
subsystems.role: a long, controlled magnetic tube that carries the lifted material away without it dispersing.

subsystems.name: Separation and storage
subsystems.role: the hydrogen and helium are separated from the rarer heavier elements that are actually worth mining.

subsystems.name: Control system
subsystems.role: keeps the star and the extraction stream stable, and lets the rate be throttled or stopped.

subsystems.name: Directed exhaust (optional)
subsystems.role: if the lifted plasma is thrown one way, the star recoils the other way, acting as an engine.

buildSteps.title: Model a candidate star
buildSteps.detail: Mass, rotation, surface magnetic field and convection patterns must be measured over years; star lifting is only conceivable on a well-understood, quietly rotating star.

buildSteps.title: Build the power supply
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a swarm of light-collecting platforms near the star, because no planet-scale energy source could drive the extraction.

buildSteps.title: Place the tap
buildSteps.detail: Superconducting coils are positioned to connect to the star's own field lines, so plasma can be drawn off along them rather than being fought against.

buildSteps.title: Heat a patch of the surface
buildSteps.detail: Low-density outer plasma is raised above escape temperature by beamed energy or radio-frequency heating, letting it flow out along the guide field.

buildSteps.title: Guide the flow
buildSteps.detail: A magnetic channel accelerates the escaping plasma and stops it from falling back; the flow rate is regulated by adjusting coil currents and heating.

buildSteps.title: Separate and store
buildSteps.detail: Far from the star the plasma is cooled, hydrogen and helium are split off from heavier isotopes, and useful material is stored in tanks or depots.

buildSteps.title: Move the material
buildSteps.detail: Electromagnetic launchers or plasma drives push the collected mass to where it is needed — a planet, a construction site, or another star.

buildSteps.title: Regulate the star
buildSteps.detail: Mass loss is monitored continuously; done slowly, removing the outer layers of a low-mass star lowers its burn rate and lengthens its life. On a massive star, whether removing mass fast enough would prevent a supernova is unproven.

prerequisites.why: high-temperature superconducting magnets work in the laboratory, but the field volumes needed here are many orders of magnitude larger.
a single star's output must be harvested on a vast scale before matter can be lifted from it.
solar probes measure the Sun's fields, but predicting where a magnetic tap could hold is not yet possible.

prerequisites.tech: Materials surviving near-stellar heat and radiation
prerequisites.why: nothing built today can operate for long in that environment.

prerequisites.tech: Self-replicating or fully autonomous space industry
prerequisites.why: the construction scale rules out hands-on assembly.

pathway.milestone: theory only: published astroengineering concepts such as the Shkadov thruster and Caplan's stellar engine
pathway.unlocks: a physics-based picture of how a star could be moved or mined.

pathway.milestone: deeper solar observation and in-situ probes of magnetic reconnection
pathway.unlocks: the field measurements any magnetic tap would depend on.

pathway.milestone: large space-based power and asteroid-material industries
pathway.unlocks: the manufacturing base and energy supply a stellar-scale project needs.

pathway.milestone: a working magnetic tap on a chosen star, then controlled mass loss
pathway.unlocks: stellar-life extension, helium-3 and metal mining, and eventually slow star-moving engines.
